summary: Al Dhafra Air Base (DHF/OMAM) is a military airbase situated in the Al Dhafra region of the United Arab Emirates, approximately 30 km south of Abu Dhabi city. The facility serves as a key installation for the UAE Air Force and hosts foreign military units, including United States Air Force personnel deployed under bilateral defense agreements. The base operates a single main runway capable of handling large military transport and fighter aircraft, and it occasionally supports limited civilian and charter operations.
faqs:
Q: Is Al Dhafra Air Base open to commercial flights?
A: No, it is primarily a military installation and does not offer scheduled commercial passenger services.

Q: Can civilians access the base?
A: Access is generally restricted to authorized military personnel, contractors, and pre-approved visitors with proper credentials.

Q: What military units are stationed at Al Dhafra?
A: The base hosts UAE Air Force squadrons and has been a major hub for US Air Force and allied coalition operations in the region.

Q: Are there any nearby civilian airports?
A: Yes, Abu Dhabi International Airport (AUH) is located roughly 30 km to the north and handles all major commercial traffic in the emirate.
transport_tips: Travelers with business at the base typically require military-arranged transport, as there is no public transit serving the facility. Private vehicles and authorized military shuttles from Abu Dhabi are the most common ways to reach the base. The drive from Abu Dhabi city center takes roughly 30 to 40 minutes via the E11 highway heading south.
local_tip: If you are arriving for a military assignment or contractor work, confirm your entry clearance and sponsor details at least 48 hours in advance, as security procedures at Al Dhafra are strict and gate entry without prior coordination is not possible.
